translationRepairs: Book of Sui, 79th year of Volume, 44th year of Biographies
s0001 is 隋書卷七十九列傳第四十四: 卷 and 列傳 mark volume and biography numbers, not years. '79th/44th year of' invents wording absent from the Chinese; Volume 79, Biographies 44 matches the title formula.

When Emperor Wu of Zhou entered the passes, Xin left his parents, wife, and children behind and went west to Chang'an, rising to high office; Luo was left behind and taken prisoner by the Northern Qi.
When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Xin left his parents, wife, and children behind and went west to Chang'an, rising to high office; Luo was left behind and taken prisoner by the Gao clan.
After 初仕魏, the text has only 武帝之入關也, not 周武帝; 信後仕周 follows later, so 'of Zhou' is an invented polity. The prisoner clause is 為高氏所囚, which is the Gao clan, not the gloss 'Northern Qi'.

When Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou entered the passes, Xin abandoned his parents, wife, and children and returned west to Chang'an, passing through offices of eminent rank; because of this Luo was thereupon taken prisoner by the Gao clan.

When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Xin abandoned his parents, wife, and children and returned west to Chang'an, passing through offices of eminent rank; because of this Luo was thereupon taken prisoner by the Gao clan.
The Chinese reads 武帝之入關也 in a Wei-service sequence (s0034 仕魏; Zhou service only at s0036). Adding 'of Northern Zhou' is unsupported by 武帝 here; stripping that gloss restores the text.
That year Cong sent Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen's An commandery but failed and returned.
That year Cong sent Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen's Gong'an but failed and returned.
襲陳公安 names the place 公安 (Gong'an), not a commandery 安. 'An commandery' mis-parses the toponym; Chen's Gong'an is accurate.
That year Cong sent the Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen's An commandery but failed and returned.
That year Cong sent the Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen Gong'an but failed and returned.
Literal likewise misread 公安 as 'An commandery'. The target is Gong'an under Chen; Chen Gong'an matches 陳公安.
Su said, "The Qian'er are Diang; the Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"
Su said, "The Qian'er are Qiang; the Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"
素曰：「鉗耳，羌也」: 羌 is the ethnonym Qiang. 'Diang' is a mistranscription with no basis in the character.
Su said, "Qian'er are Diang; Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"
Su said, "Qian'er are Qiang; Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"
The literal quotes the same 羌; Qiang is the correct reading, Diang is erroneous.
Su meant that barbarians ranked above the Diang.
Su meant that barbarians ranked above the Qiang.
素意以虜優羌劣 uses 羌, so the ranked group is the Qiang, not 'Diang'.
Su's meaning was that barbarians were superior and Diang inferior.
Su's meaning was that barbarians were superior and Qiang inferior.
Literal mirrors 羌劣; Qiang is required and Diang is wrong.
Cong said, "That the Diang differ from barbarians is something I have never heard before."
Cong said, "That the Qiang differ from barbarians is something I have never heard before."
琮曰：「以羌異虜」 again has 羌; Cong's reply concerns the Qiang, not Diang.
Cong said, "That Diang differ from barbarians is something never heard of before."
Cong said, "That Qiang differ from barbarians is something never heard of before."
The literal must render 羌 as Qiang; Diang invents a different name.
The emperor referred the case to the high officials. Duke Niuzhang Niu Hong said, "Such evil rises through men. Kill the man and it will end."
The emperor referred the case to the high officials. Niu Hong, Duke of Qizhang, said, "Such evil rises through men. Kill the man and it will end."
奇章公牛弘 is title 奇章公 plus name 牛弘. 'Duke Niuzhang' fuses and rearranges the fief title with the surname; Niu Hong, Duke of Qizhang is the correct parse.
